# Gustave Eiffel

Alexandre Gustave Eiffel (15 December 1832 — 27 December 1923) was a French civil engineer.
A graduate of École Centrale des Arts et Manufactures, he made his name with various bridges
for the French railway network, most famously the Garabit Viaduct.

## Career

Eiffel's reputation as a bridge builder was established with the construction of the
Bordeaux Bridge (1858) and later the Garabit Viaduct (1884), a railway bridge
near Ruynes-en-Margeride.

## Eiffel Tower

He is best known for the world-famous Eiffel Tower, designed by his company and built
for the 1889 Universal Exposition in Paris, and his contribution to building
the Statue of Liberty in New York.

## Later life

After his retirement from engineering, Eiffel focused on research into meteorology
and aerodynamics, making significant contributions in those fields.
